semantic.key: Gmail compose automation full working pattern
semantic.value: Gmail compose body is a contenteditable div with TrustedHTML CSP. innerHTML assignment throws TrustedHTML error. execCommand('insertText') returns true but may silently discard text. createTextNode+appendChild works but Gmail may not register as user input (saves as draft instead of sending). RELIABLE PATTERN: (1) Start daemon headed with visible window — this is the #1 prerequisite. (2) type for To field (input[aria-label='To recipients']) + press Enter. (3) type for Subject (input[name=subjectbox]). (4) click body div[aria-label='Message Body'] (use --force=true if visibility fails). (5) eval --file with execCommand('selectAll') then execCommand('insertText', false, text). (6) Verify body: eval 'el.innerText.length'. (7) Send: press Control+Enter. (8) Verify sent: document.title returns to inbox. If window not visible, ALL click/type commands timeout — this was the root cause of a 30-min debugging disaster on 2026-07-28.

semantic.key: DeepSeek PoW algorithm (DeepSeekHashV1) fully cracked
semantic.value: DeepSeekHashV1 = SHA3-256 with Keccak-f[1600] round 0 SKIPPED (23 rounds instead of standard 24). Input: f"{salt}_{expire_at}_{nonce}".encode() (plain ASCII string, NO hex decoding). Check: deepseek_hash_v1(input) == bytes.fromhex(challenge) — EXACT 32-byte equality, not leading-zeros. Server generates challenge by picking random nonce in [0, difficulty), hashing it, sending hash. Client brute-forces same range. difficulty=144000 typical. Pure Python ~50s, WASM ~100ms, Go ~50ms.

semantic.key: DeepSeek SSE content extraction pattern
semantic.value: SSE stream content assembly: First data event contains full initial fragment at v.response.fragments[0].content (e.g. 'Hello'). Subsequent content chunks are JSON patches: {"p":"response/fragments/-1/content","o":"APPEND","v":" chunk"}. Concatenate initial + all APPEND v values for full response. Stream end markers: {"p":"response/status","o":"SET","v":"FINISHED"} then 'event: close'. Title event gives auto-generated session title.

semantic.key: DeepSeek session creation endpoint
semantic.value: POST https://chat.deepseek.com/api/v0/chat_session/create with empty JSON body {} and Bearer token returns {data:{biz_data:{id:'uuid'}}}. The id is used as chat_session_id in completion requests. No other parameters needed. Each completion call can use a fresh session or reuse existing ones.

semantic.key: Sable DeepSeek model routing architecture
semantic.value: DeepSeek models (Expert/Instant/Vision) are first-class entries in engine/config.py MODELS list with api_backend:'deepseek' and api_model_type field. server.py routes via _is_deepseek_api_model(model_id) which checks get_model_config(model_id).get('api_backend')=='deepseek' + token availability. Routing order (non-stream): scraper_enabled → browser scraper; _is_deepseek_api_model → HTTP API client; fallback → built-in Qwen service. Stream path same priority. The old _use_deepseek_api() scraper-settings-based hijack was removed — routing is now per-model, not per-scraper-state.

semantic.key: DeepSeek model_type values for Sable dropdown
semantic.value: Three DeepSeek models in config.py: deepseek-expert (api_model_type='expert'), deepseek-instant (api_model_type=None, serializes as JSON null), deepseek-vision (api_model_type='vision'). Each has Fast + Thinking modes. The client's thinking_enabled check is case-insensitive: str(thinking_mode).lower() in ('thinking','deepthink'). model_type=None must NOT be coerced to 'default' — Instant requires literal null in the request body.

semantic.key: DeepSeek session continuity via parent_message_id counter
semantic.value: DeepSeek conversations use integer parent_message_id: first message sends null, then 2, 4, 6, 8... (increments by 2 each turn — user msg gets odd id, assistant gets even). DeepSeekClient._sessions dict maps sable_chat_id → (deepseek_session_id, next_parent_id). _prepare_request(chat_id) reuses existing session or creates new. _advance_session() called on FINISHED event increments counter. Server passes chat_id=active_chat_id to both chat() and stream_chat().

When modifying Sable DB helper functions to access new columns: always check that the SELECT statement explicitly includes the column name before accessing via row["col"]. SQLite Row objects only contain columns listed in SELECT — accessing an unlisted column raises IndexError/KeyError causing 500s. Grep for the SELECT query when extending existing functions.

procedural.key: Diagnosing Python process memory bloat on Linux
procedural.value: When a Python process uses excessive RAM: 1) grep VmRSS/VmPeak /proc/PID/status for overview. 2) cat /proc/PID/smaps_rollup for Rss/Pss/AnonHugePages breakdown. 3) Parse /proc/PID/maps to find large anonymous mappings (>100MB) — single huge anon mmaps indicate allocator arenas (ONNX, numpy, jemalloc). 4) Compare RSS vs VmPeak: big gap means allocation-then-free pattern (arena pre-allocation). 5) Check loaded .so files via grep on maps to identify the library. 6) For ONNX specifically: disable enable_cpu_mem_arena in SessionOptions.

procedural.key: Avoiding shell quoting in browser eval commands
procedural.value: When running JS via browser_control eval: (1) If JS has NO double quotes: eval 'document.title' works directly. (2) If JS has quotes/newlines/emoji: write JS to file via heredoc with QUOTED delimiter (cat > /tmp/x.js << 'JSEOF' ... JSEOF), then either: eval --file /tmp/x.js, or B64=$(base64 -w0 /tmp/x.js) && eval "b64:$B64". (3) NEVER retry with different quote arrangements after a SyntaxError — it's always shell quoting, switch to file/b64 immediately. (4) The heredoc delimiter MUST be quoted ('JSEOF') to prevent shell expansion of $ and backticks inside the JS.

When click/type/hover timeout with 'element is not visible': (1) First check: eval 'document.title' — if this works but click doesn't, the window is hidden/minimized. (2) Check: dump_html 'selector' — if element exists in HTML but click fails, it's a visibility issue not a missing element. (3) Fix option A: restart daemon headed, ensure window is on current workspace. (4) Fix option B: use --force=true on the command (skips all safety checks). (5) NEVER retry the same click/type more than once — if it times out twice, it's environmental, not a selector issue. (6) Screenshot + get_file to visually confirm page state before further debugging.

Use tokei (pacman -S tokei) for accurate language-aware line counts. It auto-excludes binary blobs, node_modules, cached browser data, and other non-code artifacts. find+wc -l picks up everything and inflates counts dramatically (12x in Sable's case). For large projects, run in background (bg='true') — inline find+wc times out at 15s.

Fast path: use wasmtime with /tmp/sha3_wasm.wasm (100ms) or compile Go solver from shaohuahuawww/deepseek-pow (50ms). Slow path: pure Python hash_impl.py (~50s for difficulty=144000). Algorithm: prefix = f'{salt}_{expire_at}_'.encode(); for nonce in range(difficulty): if deepseek_hash_v1(prefix + str(nonce).encode()) == bytes.fromhex(challenge): return nonce. The hash is SHA3-256 sponge with _keccak_f23 (rounds 1-23, skipping round 0). Build response: base64(JSON{algorithm, challenge, salt, answer, signature, target_path}). Send as X-DS-PoW-Response header.

procedural.key: Full DeepSeek chat completion flow (verified working)
procedural.value: Complete working sequence: (1) TOKEN=$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.loads(localStorage.getItem('userToken'))['value'])") from browser eval. (2) curl POST /api/v0/chat/create_pow_challenge with Bearer token + {target_path:'/api/v0/chat/completion'} → get challenge JSON. (3) echo challenge_json | /home/sifat/hdd/projects/Sable/connectors/deepseek/pow_solver/pow_solver → nonce. (4) Build pow_header = base64(json{algorithm,challenge,salt,answer:nonce,signature,target_path}). (5) POST /api/v0/chat_session/create with {} → session_id. (6) POST /api/v0/chat/completion with headers (Authorization, X-DS-PoW-Response, x-client-version:2.3.0, x-client-platform:web, x-client-bundle-id:com.deepseek.chat, x-client-locale:en_US) + body {chat_session_id, parent_message_id:null, model_type:'default', prompt, ref_file_ids:[], thinking_enabled:false, search_enabled:false, action:null, preempt:false}. Response is SSE text/event-stream.
